title: Adaptive Model Saltation: short-horizon competitor probes & procurement-signal catalog
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Build a compact, repeatable playbook to detect short-horizon competitor model behavior (releases, tight quantization variants, pricing shocks) and translate those signals into procurement-ready triggers and an onramp candidate catalog for Dedicated/Private. This ticket scopes the investigative probes, success metrics, rubric for a procurement-readiness score, and the initial automation plan for daily signal harvesting.
acceptance_criteria: A documented probe matrix with 6 competitor endpoints and 3 synthetic workloads (chat, long-context summarization, embeddings).
A procurement-readiness rubric (5 dimensions) and a scoring spreadsheet with population of at least 12 model-variant observations.
Automation prototype that runs nightly probes, stores latency/cost/behaviour snapshots, and surfaces top-3 fallback candidates for two customer personas (latency-first, price-sensitive).
Stakeholder signoff from Go-to-market and Solutions Engineering on scoring thresholds for sales triggers.
tasks: Finalize probe matrix: endpoints, payload templates, rate limits
Create synthetic workload templates (short chat, 2.5k-token summarization, 512-dim embeddings queries)
Define procurement-readiness rubric: availability, latency variance, quant-fidelity, cost per token, API stability
Implement nightly probe runner (prototype) and S3 bucket for snapshots
Populate initial dataset and run analysis on 2026-02-24 to 2026-03-02 window
Draft one-page decision guide for Sales & Solutions on when to recommend Dedicated reserve vs Hosted fallback
Present findings in Model Supply Intelligence sync and capture feedback
comments: 2026-03-03 - Diego Ramirez: Kickoff complete. Aligned on 6 competitor endpoints (two open models, two cloud provider hosted endpoints, two smaller specialty vendors). Assigned probe ownership: Diego -> host probes, Mina -> embeddings templates.
2026-03-05 - Mina Chen (Solutions Eng): Early observation: one competitor toggled a quantized-8 path mid-week causing 18% lower cost for same prompt; need to capture variant metadata in snapshots.
2026-03-07 - Asha Patel: Added procurement-readiness rubric draft to Confluence. Requesting GTM and Sales thresholds by 2026-03-12.

2026-03-09 - Diego Ramirez: Prototype runner deployed. Nightly runs capturing latency p95, p99, token-cost estimate, and response-stability hash. Initial run produced 14 observations; flagged two variants as high-opportunity for fallback testing.

2026-03-10 - Benji Morales (GTM): Reviewed scoring rubric; requested a conservative threshold for latency-first customers and a different threshold for price-sensitive customers. Added to acceptance criteria for signoff.
updates: 2026-03-04 - Probe matrix finalized; included regional endpoints (us-east, eu-west).
2026-03-06 - Workload templates uploaded to Drive; embeddings batch sizes set to 64 for consistency.
2026-03-08 - Rubric iteration 2: replaced 'API stability' with 'variant volatility' to reflect sudden tuning changes.
2026-03-10 - Prototype runner now tags snapshot entries with observed quantization hints and HTTP headers for provenance.
risks: Probe rate limits may lead to temporary IP blocks; mitigation: staggered runs and provider API keys
Competitor endpoints may return non-deterministic responses; mitigation: response-stability hashing and multiple repeats
Legal/ToS considerations for probing public endpoints; mitigation: consult Legal before scaling probes
notes: This ticket is intentionally compact: the goal is to produce a repeatable signal->score pipeline in two sprints so that Sales can be alerted when a viable low-cost fallback appears. We will iterate the rubric after GTM feedback.
